messages:
elaine: Quick heads-up — I'm planning a staggered publish for the Python + TS SDKs tonight during the 01:00 UTC change window. Need sign-off on pin strategy and the deprecation blurb for the sync client.
raj: Are we still doing the 10% canary -> 50% -> 100% traffic steps? Any new rollback criteria?
tim: yes, that's the plan. Rollback if >1% error delta on 5m or any packaging/signature mismatch on pip/npm.
elaine: Deploy-bot will run the publish. I'll tag releases 2.4.0 (py) and 2.4.0 (ts) and set dist-tags: "canary-nightdrop" first. If canary is green we'll shift dist-tag to "next" then "latest".
ana: small nit: for enterprise customers we should pin the older major (1.x) in the release notes and explicitly call out breaking changes.
raj: Agreed. Add a short migration snippet for the sync->async change. Also include the opt-out flag for legacy apps: --use-legacy-sync.
tim: I'll monitor telemetry dash (route: /sdk/*) and watch for latency regressions. Will signal with :thumbsup: if green.
deploy-bot: publish job started — building wheels and tarballs for python 2.4.0. npm pack for ts 2.4.0 queued.
elaine: FYI packing step sometimes hits transient 429s to registry. Plan: if pack fails, deploy-bot will retry with exponential backoff up to 5 attempts, then pause and @raj + @tim get notified.
raj: If that happens, we should avoid promoting dist-tags automatically. Manual gate required if registry errors appear.
ana: Also we should pin the new SDK in the internal examples repo to a canary tag, not latest, until 24h of smoke tests.
tim: Good call. I'll hold the docs cutover until after canary -> next. Docs PR: https://git.internal/docs/sdk/2.4.0 (draft)
elaine: Draft release notes snippet (short): "2.4.0: Introduces async-first client APIs, improved batching defaults, and telemetry opt-in. Deprecates sync client v1.* — see migration notes." Thoughts?
raj: Fine. Add a callout: "If you rely on sync client behavior please use --use-legacy-sync and upgrade within 90 days."
ana: Add a code example showing the async pattern + small FAQ entry about connection pooling.
deploy-bot: python publish finished: wheels uploaded to PyPI (verifier: ok). npm pack succeeded. Starting canary dist-tag flip to canary-nightdrop.
elaine: Starting canary traffic now (10%). Tim, watch errors/latency for the next 15 minutes, then we'll move to 50% if green.
tim: Watching. No spikes so far (0/15m). :thumbsup:
elaine: Moving to 50%.
deploy-bot: Dist-tag moved to "next"; canary -> next transition complete.
raj: Observability green. One minor warning in telemetry about a deprecated field; filing a follow-up but not blocking.
elaine: OK promote to latest in 10m. If anyone sees anything weird call a hold. Otherwise we'll publish release notes + announce in #general after final.
ana: I'll lock internal examples to the canary tag and open the docs PR for final tweaks.
elaine: Final promote now. Release notes published: https://internal.releases/redwood-sdk/2.4.0
tim: Confirming no client regressions from synthetic tests. :white_check_mark:
elaine: Thanks all. Postmortem if we need one. If deploy-bot encountered >3 retries on registry step we would have aborted and rolled back — recorded as rollback policy in the runbook.
raj: One action item: update the release-runbook to add the --use-legacy-sync flag in examples and include the npm backoff thresholds.
ana: I'll raise a small docs PR and link it in the runbook.
elaine: Closing thread. :tada:
